p: Southend is one of the easiest seaside trips from London. Trains run into both Southend Central and Southend Victoria, and both are a walk from the seafront, so leaving the car at home saves you a hunt for parking on hot days.

Here's a simple way to shape the day. Start on the rides while it's quieter in the morning, especially the bigger ones with the longest queues. Break for chips or an ice cream and an hour on the beach, then head back to Adventure Island in the afternoon for a second round. Splitting it up keeps everyone's energy going and stops the day turning into one long queue.
Measure the kids before you go so you can work out which wristband actually makes sense, and keep valuables zipped up or in a locker on the faster rides. Loose items have a habit of going flying.

If you've got time, Southend Pier is right next door and stretches way out into the Thames Estuary, with its own little railway to save your legs on the return trip. A short hop along the coast, Old Leigh is a lovely contrast to the bright lights, with cockle sheds, seafood stalls and fishing boats bobbing about in the creek. It's a great spot for a quieter end to the day.
Pack sun cream, because the beach and the rides are mostly out in the open, and a light jacket for when the wind picks up off the estuary later on.
